subject: technology

rubric.exceeds: Every step, value, or rendered choice is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with no notable errors.
rubric.meets: The work is accurate and faithful to the stated criteria, with at most one minor self-correctable error.
rubric.developing: The work is mostly accurate but has one or more errors that change the result or the intended effect.
rubric.beginning: Multiple accuracy or fidelity errors prevent the work from meeting the stated criteria.

rubric.exceeds: Test cases include normal, boundary, and deliberate-break inputs, each with expected against actual recorded and every failure resolved and re-run.
rubric.meets: The required cases were run with expected against actual recorded, and failures were addressed.
rubric.developing: Some checking occurred but cases are too few, results are unrecorded, or a known failure was left unresolved.
rubric.beginning: The work was submitted without evidence it was checked against any case.

rubric.exceeds: Design choices are justified against a named alternative, with the trade-off stated in terms of the actual requirement.
rubric.meets: Design choices are explained with a stated reason.
rubric.developing: Choices are described but the reasoning is generic or does not connect to the requirement.

rubric.exceeds: A documented revision traces symptom to cause to fix to passing check, and a pattern across errors is named with a countermeasure.
rubric.meets: At least one real revision is documented with what changed and how improvement can be told.
rubric.developing: A change was made but the cause or the evidence of improvement is missing.
rubric.beginning: No evidence the work was revisited or corrected.

scoring_judgment_guidance: Score this session with the rubric below, not against a fixed answer key — a design, code, or debugging task legitimately has more than one valid solution. Score only what a build and test on gathering feedback can show: this is one increment of progress, so score the increment and its documentation rather than the unfinished whole. Record the level reached on each dimension with one specific reason drawn from the actual submission. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about gathering feedback.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about gathering feedback; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

accepted_evidence_model: The response accurately links at least three printed details to gathering feedback.
The proposed revision or decision is feasible within the supplied fictional case and does not invent missing facts.
The pass condition is observable, specific, and tests the proposed revision rather than restating a preference.
The limitation or trade-off correctly identifies what the supplied evidence cannot establish.
protected_task.decisive_resolution: Accept multiple defensible responses. A passing response has three traceable evidence links, one feasible revision or decision, one observable check, and one honest limitation; reject claims that require facts outside the package.
protected_task.prohibited_shortcut: Do not give the learner a completed evidence map, selected decision, or finished design before independent evidence is submitted.

accepted_evidence_model: Each claim cites N1–N5 and stays within what that label supports.
The revision addresses N5 while continuing to respect N1 and N2.
The pass condition is observable and could disconfirm the learner’s preferred revision.
The limitation names an unresolved question rather than inventing an answer.
fresh_mastery_check.decisive_resolution: Accept multiple responses that satisfy all four evidence conditions; no single wording, layout, or decision is required.

remediation_authority.selection_rule: Choose the smallest alternate route from observable evidence; do not repeat the original task or expose its protected resolution.
remediation_authority.mastery_reconsideration: Reconsider mastery only from the fresh independent record under the same criteria. A worked or guided response is instruction, not mastery evidence.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use digital artifact, algorithm or code, test log, source record, design explanation, and safe-use reflection; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.

mastery_interpretation.secure: At least 85% with accurate independent application and adequate evidence/reasoning.
mastery_interpretation.developing: 70–84% or inconsistent explanation; assign targeted review and a fresh transfer check.
mastery_interpretation.not_yet: Below 70% or a missing prerequisite; reteach the smallest gap and reassess with new evidence.
mastery_interpretation.rule: A unit score is one evidence source, not the sole basis for long-term mastery.

unit_assessment_reference.note: This lesson is one session inside the unit; the unit assessment record above is the summative instrument, and this lesson rubric scores only this session's evidence.

remediation_plan: Reteaching for gathering feedback follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for gathering feedback, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for gathering feedback works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of gathering feedback, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking gathering feedback mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension_plan: Apply gathering feedback under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on gathering feedback rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
accommodation_note: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: You can do this with the keyboard only, no mouse needed. Text can be made bigger, and you may do it on paper instead of a screen.
This work takes more than one sitting. Ask for a simple checklist with dates so you know what to do next. Keeping track is not part of your grade.
You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.
parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.

safety_and_privacy.note: No real credential, live external system, production account, or real personal data is used anywhere in this session; all values are fictional or sandboxed and no live system may be probed or accessed.
